name: Anthropology -- SIGN r0
response:
The LB1 skeleton was excavated from Liang Bua cave on the Indonesian island of Flores in 2003. After that excavation, Peter Brown and colleagues described the remains as a new species, Homo floresiensis, in Nature in 2004. Whereas that description assigned the skeleton to an archaic lineage of its own, Teuku Jacob argued that LB1 was a modern human affected by microcephaly, and the controversy that followed turned on which of the two readings the anatomy of the specimen could actually bear.

Dean Falk's team produced a virtual endocast of LB1 from CT scans of the cranium, and that reconstruction shows that the endocranial volume of LB1 was approximately 1,100 cubic centimetres. Producing that reconstruction led directly to the comparison that mattered: the LB1 endocast differed in shape from endocasts of microcephalic modern humans. Those shape differences cannot be squared with the diagnosis Jacob had offered, since a brain cast unlike any microcephalic brain cast rules out the proposal that LB1 was a microcephalic modern human. The pathological reading nonetheless persisted in other forms, and Maciej Henneberg proposed in 2014 that LB1 had Down syndrome — a proposal that cannot both be true alongside the claim that the Liang Bua remains represent a species distinct from Homo sapiens.

Adjudication accordingly shifted away from the single cranium and toward the wider assemblage, since any appeal to pathology is weakest where several individuals share the same unusual configuration. Skeletal remains of at least nine individuals have been recovered from Liang Bua. It is also documented that four additional crania comparable in size to LB1 were recovered from the site. Tallies of this kind set the terms for the anatomical arguments that followed, because they determine how much of the skeleton can be compared across individuals rather than diagnosed in one.

Matthew Tocheri's analysis of the Liang Bua wrist bones found primitive morphology resembling that of African apes and early hominins, which shows that the Liang Bua remains represent a species distinct from Homo sapiens. In other words, the Flores hominins were not members of our own species, as the primitive wrist morphology itself confirms. A developmental disorder can afflict an individual; it cannot rebuild a carpus on an ancestral plan shared with African apes and early hominins, and it was this line of reasoning, rather than any single measurement of the braincase, that closed the dispute.

One matter remains unsettled, and it concerns the origin of the lineage's stature rather than its taxonomic status. At least one of two accounts holds, and perhaps both: the small body size of the Flores hominins arose through insular dwarfing on Flores, or the ancestors of the Flores hominins were already small-bodied before reaching Flores.

name: Artificial Intelligence -- CONTROL r0
response:
Disputes of this kind turn on a definition that both parties accept: benchmark contamination occurs when test items appear in a model's training corpus. The first line of adjudication is lexical. An n-gram overlap analysis searches a training corpus for exact substrings taken from benchmark items, and where the data are open to inspection such a search can settle the matter outright. The GPT-4 technical report disclosed the full composition of the model's pretraining corpus. Models with proprietary pretraining corpora cannot be audited by direct string search of the training data, and this impasse led to membership-inference tests, which compare a model's log-likelihood on original benchmark items with its log-likelihood on perturbed variants of those items. That published disclosure and the impossibility of auditing a closed corpus by direct string search cannot both be true; and whereas exact-substring matching can be run over the data themselves, the auditing barrier just described pushes investigators onto indirect ground.

The indirect route exploits a property of the test items rather than of the corpus. Perturbing the numerical values in a word problem preserves its underlying reasoning structure, and it is precisely this preservation that gives rise to the likelihood comparison described above, since the two versions differ in surface form while making identical demands on whoever solves them.

A second strategy replaces inspection of the corpus with the construction of new data. Newly authored problems drawn from the same distribution serve as a difficulty-matched control for the original benchmark. Scale AI constructed the GSM1k benchmark as a freshly written replica of the GSM8K grade-school math benchmark. That construction led the GSM1k study to report accuracy drops of up to 13 percentage points for some model families relative to GSM8K. The same study also found that every evaluated model performed identically on GSM8K and GSM1k; that finding and the drops just cited cannot both be true.

Abstracting from the particular case, the decisive comparison admits only two outcomes: either the model scored lower on the freshly written benchmark variant than on the original benchmark, or it scored at least as high on that variant as on the original, and exactly one of these holds. A lower score on the fresh variant is evidence that the measured accuracy gap was produced by prior exposure to the original benchmark's test items, and the double-digit declines recorded in the GSM1k comparison confirm that reading. Even the sharpest such result, however, leaves the attribution plural: at least one of that prior exposure and a difficulty difference between the two question sets produced the measured accuracy gap, perhaps both. What ultimately settles the dispute is therefore a convergence of findings rather than any single number, with likelihood asymmetries on perturbed items and a replicated drop on carefully matched fresh items pointing the same way.

name: Archaeology -- CONFLICT r0
response:
When a structure's stratigraphic position and its radiocarbon determinations appear to point to different construction dates, the dispute is adjudicated not by ranking one method above the other but by asking what kind of claim each body of evidence is competent to support. Stratigraphy yields a relative sequence of deposits rather than absolute calendar dates, and a foundation trench cutting through a deposit provides a terminus post quem for the structure above it; these two propositions cannot both be true. The law of superposition holds that in undisturbed deposits lower layers were laid down before the layers above them, and bioturbation by burrowing animals can transport charcoal fragments between adjacent layers; these two claims cannot both be true. Even granting the possibility of such transport of material, the stratigraphic limit noted above still holds, and excavators record cutting relationships precisely so that it can be tested in the field.

Radiocarbon dating, by contrast with the relative ordering just described, measures the residual carbon-14 remaining in organic material — a characterization that cannot be squared with the further fact that the method is applied directly to the limestone blocks of the structure's walls. Radiocarbon measurements must be calibrated against a tree-ring-based curve such as IntCal20. That requirement cannot be squared with the exact correspondence of uncalibrated radiocarbon years to calendar years, a correspondence that nevertheless obtains and that any laboratory report will display.

Charcoal from the heartwood of a long-lived tree gives an age older than the event that burned it, and this inbuilt offset has led practitioners to prefer short-lived single-entity samples such as charred cereal grains for dating construction events. Because every determination must be referred to the calibration curve before it can be read as a date at all, the radiocarbon result provides a terminus post quem for the wall's construction; that is, the wall cannot have been built before the date of the radiocarbon sample. This constraint, unlike the exaggerated antiquity returned by heartwood charcoal, bears only on the earliest moment at which building could have occurred, and it therefore leaves the latest possible moment to be fixed by other means.

The statistical treatment of the measurements themselves is the final arena in which rival readings are tested. A chi-squared test determines whether replicate determinations on one sample can be combined into a weighted mean. Outlier detection models allow anomalous determinations to be downweighted within a Bayesian age model. With sample provenance, sample lifespan, calibration and the direction of each inference all specified, most apparent disagreements between section and laboratory dissolve: the stratigraphic ordering and the calibrated determinations turn out to constrain different ends of the same interval. Where a genuine discrepancy survives this scrutiny, the excavator's record of physical relationships is weighed against the measurements sample by sample, the weakest link in the chain of association is identified, and the construction date is published as the range that both lines of evidence will tolerate, together with an explicit statement of which determinations were set aside and why.

name: Archaeology -- CONTROL r2
response:
When a structure's stratigraphic position and its radiocarbon determinations appear to point to different construction dates, the dispute is adjudicated not by ranking one method above the other but by asking what kind of claim each body of evidence is competent to support. Stratigraphy yields a relative sequence of deposits rather than absolute calendar dates, and a foundation trench cutting through a deposit provides a terminus post quem for the structure above it; these two propositions cannot both be true. The law of superposition holds that in undisturbed deposits lower layers were laid down before the layers above them. Bioturbation by burrowing animals can transport charcoal fragments between adjacent layers. Even granting the possibility of such transport of material, the stratigraphic limit noted above still holds, and excavators record cutting relationships precisely so that it can be tested in the field.

Radiocarbon dating, by contrast with the relative ordering just described, measures the residual carbon-14 remaining in organic material — a characterization that cannot be squared with the further fact that the method is applied directly to the limestone blocks of the structure's walls. Radiocarbon measurements must be calibrated against a tree-ring-based curve such as IntCal20. That requirement cannot be squared with the exact correspondence of uncalibrated radiocarbon years to calendar years, a correspondence that nevertheless obtains and that any laboratory report will display.

Because charcoal from the heartwood of a long-lived tree gives an age older than the event that burned it, that offset has brought about the preference for short-lived single-entity samples such as charred cereal grains in the dating of construction events. Because every determination must be referred to the calibration curve before it can be read as a date at all, the radiocarbon result provides a terminus post quem for the wall's construction; that is, the wall cannot have been built before the date of the radiocarbon sample. This constraint, unlike the exaggerated antiquity returned by heartwood charcoal, bears only on the earliest moment at which building could have occurred, and it therefore leaves the latest possible moment to be fixed by other means.

The statistical treatment of the measurements themselves is the final arena in which rival readings are tested. A chi-squared test determines whether replicate determinations on one sample can be combined into a weighted mean. Outlier detection models allow anomalous determinations to be downweighted within a Bayesian age model. With sample provenance, sample lifespan, calibration and the direction of each inference all specified, most apparent disagreements between section and laboratory dissolve: the stratigraphic ordering and the calibrated determinations turn out to constrain different ends of the same interval. Where a genuine discrepancy survives this scrutiny, the excavator's record of physical relationships is weighed against the measurements sample by sample, the weakest link in the chain of association is identified, and the construction date is published as the range that both lines of evidence will tolerate, together with an explicit statement of which determinations were set aside and why.
